:::danger[Zero is being retired — historical reference]
Zero / zero-cache / ZQL named-queries / WebSocket push is **on the retirement
path**. The shipping desktop app uses **SSE-primary** sync (the `:3070` Hono
host pushes invalidate/update over Postgres `LISTEN/NOTIFY`); zero-cache is
**not run** on desktop. Treat this page as historical reference. Source of
truth: `apps/operator/providers/HarnessSyncProvider.tsx` (transport-selection
doc-comment) + the root `CLAUDE.md` deployment-model section.
:::

## Database

The harness DB is `papercusp` on `localhost:5432`. (It was renamed from
`restart_harness` in April 2026 — old references will still appear in
older code.) Three Postgres roles see it:

- `harness_app` — read/write from API routes and agent code.
- `harness_admin` — DDL, used by scaffolders.
- `harness_zero` — read-only via logical replication, used by
  `zero-cache-harness`.

## Schema layout

The baseline (`libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/000-baseline.sql`) creates two
schemas, `harness_shared` and `papercup_shared`. A fully migrated DB has
**more than two** global schemas, though: migration `109-global-schemas-and-grants`
also (re)creates `papercusp_auth` (operator identity — `users`, `sessions`,
`magic_link_requests`) and `audit` (`operator_actions`, `action_executions`),
which the squashed baseline's narrow `pg_dump` had dropped, and
`papercusp_marketplace` is created at runtime by the plugin layer.

The four core per-harness entities are now **consolidated base tables in
`harness_shared`**, keyed on a `harness_slug` column; the old physical
`harness_<slug>.*` tables were dropped (archived migration
`032-drop-per-harness-tables-replace-with-views`) and replaced with
auto-updatable VIEWs for back-compat with writers that still pass a slug.
The slug is a row value, not a schema name.

```
papercusp database
├── harness_shared
│   ├── projects                            (cross-harness portfolio)
│   ├── harness_features_consolidated       (PK harness_slug, feature_id)
│   ├── harness_issues_consolidated         (PK harness_slug, issue_id)
│   ├── agent_runs_consolidated             (PK harness_slug, run_id)
│   ├── harness_snapshots_consolidated      (PK harness_slug, snapshot_id)
│   ├── agent_chats_consolidated            (PK workspace_id, harness_slug, id)
│   ├── feature_audit_consolidated          (PK id)
│   └── audit_log, harness_decisions, harness_phases, …
├── papercup_shared
│   ├── messages
│   ├── message_recipients
│   ├── message_comments
│   ├── directive_summaries
│   └── briefings
└── harness_<slug>                          (one schema per registered harness;
    ├── harness_features  (VIEW)             created at install time, NOT by the
    ├── harness_issues    (VIEW)             baseline — auto-updatable VIEWs over
    └── …                 (VIEW)             the consolidated tables, back-compat)
```

Note the per-harness back-compat VIEWs are **not** nested inside
`harness_shared`: each registered harness gets its own `harness_<slug>`
schema, created at install/scaffold time (the baseline only defines
`harness_shared`). Note also that not every consolidated table is keyed
`(harness_slug, <entity_id>)`: `agent_chats_consolidated` is also
workspace-scoped (`(workspace_id, harness_slug, id)`) and
`feature_audit_consolidated` is keyed on `id` alone.

## Consolidated tables, not schema-per-harness (Option A)

The original design was schema-per-harness ("Option B" — one
`harness_<slug>` schema with its own physical tables). That was
**reverted**: the system now uses a single consolidated table per entity
in `harness_shared` with a `harness_slug` column ("Option A"). The
physical per-harness tables were dropped (archived migration `032`) and
replaced with auto-updatable VIEWs so older slug-passing writers keep
working.

Why the switch:

- Adding a harness no longer requires DDL — the slug is a regular row
  value at install time, so there's nothing to scaffold or add to Zero.
- One hot table per entity is simpler to back up, index, and reason
  about than N near-identical per-slug copies.
- Cross-harness reads (the `/features` page, the consolidated `.all`
  queries) are a plain `WHERE` filter, not a UNION across N schemas.

Trade-off accepted: a single hot table per entity (the original concern
about replication-slot lag on one hot table) in exchange for far less
operational and DDL surface.

## Per-harness compatibility views

A `harness_<slug>` namespace, when present, is a compatibility surface. Its relations are auto-updatable VIEWs over harness_shared.*_consolidated tables filtered by harness_slug; it contains no physical per-harness entity tables.

The live helper is packages/operator-core/lib/scaffold-harness-schema.ts. The add-project and onboard flows call it to create the schema, views, grants, and safe column defaults needed by legacy slug-scoped writers. It does not render a SQL template and it does not add per-harness tables to the publication.

To change canonical storage, add an idempotent numbered migration under `libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/<NNN>-*.sql`, then refresh the schema projection with node libs/papercusp/libs/db/scripts/pull-schema.mjs. The slug is a row value in the shared table, not a physical-table namespace.
## The `zero_harness` publication

Postgres logical replication needs a `PUBLICATION` listing every table
to broadcast. Ours is named `zero_harness` and contains every relevant
table from every per-harness schema plus the shared schemas.

Inspect it:

```sql
SELECT schemaname, tablename
FROM pg_publication_tables
WHERE pubname = 'zero_harness'
ORDER BY schemaname, tablename;
```

When a new harness is registered, the TypeScript helper creates only the slug-filtered compatibility VIEWs. The canonical shared tables and their transport/publication membership are established by migrations. Adding a harness therefore does not require per-harness DDL or publication edits.

## Cross-harness consolidated tables

`harness_shared.harness_features_consolidated` is the canonical example.
It's a base table — and the **only** physical store for features. Schema:

```
harness_features_consolidated (
  harness_slug   text,
  feature_id     text,
  -- …all columns of harness_features…
  primary key (harness_slug, feature_id)
)
```

There are no per-harness base tables and no sync triggers any more. The
old design trigger-mirrored each per-harness `harness_features` table
into this consolidated table, but migration `032` dropped the per-harness
physical tables (and the `sync_*_consolidated()` trigger functions) and
replaced them with auto-updatable `harness_<slug>.harness_features` VIEWs
that are plain `SELECT *` over the consolidated table filtered by slug.
(The `harness_shared.sync_features_consolidated()` function still appears
in the baseline dump but is **not attached to any trigger** — it's
vestigial.) Writers now target the consolidated table directly, or write
through the slug-scoped view.

Adding a column means: add it to the consolidated table only. The views
are `SELECT *`, so they pick it up automatically — no per-table or
per-trigger edits.

Getting cross-harness data into Zero is straightforward as a result: the
consolidated base table is published directly (e.g.
`harness_shared.harness_features_consolidated` is a member of the
`zero_harness` publication), and the per-harness slug-scoped reads are
just VIEWs over it. (Zero itself is on the retirement path — see the
banner at the top of this page.)

## papercup_shared schema

The Papercup app (organization layer, project tracking, messaging) has
its own data that isn't per-harness. The messaging tables live in
`papercup_shared`:

- `messages` — formerly JSON, now PG-canonical
- `message_recipients`, `message_comments`, `directive_summaries`
- `briefings`

(Note: the cross-harness `projects` table lives in **`harness_shared`**,
not `papercup_shared`.)

These are read by named queries without a slug arg — `messages.*` and
`directiveSummaries.*`, plus the `messageRecipients.*`, `messageComments.*`,
and `briefings.*` namespaces (all in `libs/zero-harness/src/queries.ts`).
Cross-app code reaches them via `search_path = papercup_shared, public`
in the connection.

The old `{ "derivedFromPg": true }` JSON ledgers — file snapshots rebuilt
from PG for tooling that wanted a file — are gone from the live path. The
only code that still emits that tag lives under `_retired/` (the messaging /
briefings surface); it is not part of the live messaging path. Postgres is
the source of truth.

## Slug as the stable cross-store identifier

Project mutations use `slug` as the primary filter, not `id`. Reason:

- The JSON ledger generated UUID ids.
- Legacy PG rows used `PROJ-<slug>` ids.
- The two diverged silently for months.

Slug is unique, stable, and the only field both stores agreed on. New
mutations (`record-revenue`, `campaigns/metrics`, `PATCH /projects`) all
filter by slug. If you're writing a new mutation against `projects`,
filter by slug.
